deduplication.rule: DOI, else PMID, else normalised title (ASCII-folded, alphanumeric only)
deduplication.known_defect: build_pool.py keyed PubMed records by the last DOI in the record, which can be a cited reference; some merges are therefore wrong and some report ids in the pool are not the report's own. The ledger keys reports by verified identifiers; the pool was rebuilt on 2026-09-15 and this note is kept for the history.

second_known_defect.what: The key order is DOI, then PMID, then normalised title, so the same work entered twice whenever one database supplied a DOI and the other did not. That is common between PubMed and Scopus.
second_known_defect.effect: the unique count above is an overcount by at most records_involved minus groups; one work sits in the priority stratum twice and was screened in twice, once in each round

audit_of_unscreened_scopus_remainder.interpretation: The clear rate in this stratum is several times the rate measured in the parent remainder in September. The likely reason is that the Scopus queries name this review's subject matter directly and Scopus matches them against indexed keywords as well as title and abstract, so a record can be squarely on topic and still score below a threshold built from title and abstract words. The ordering rule and its threshold were left unchanged, because they were registered before the first screen; what changes is the size of the declared gap.
audit_of_unscreened_scopus_remainder.not_a_measured_ratio: The two strata were judged by the same assistant on different days from differently formatted listings, so the difference between the two rates is not a measurement of anything. Comparing them properly would mean judging the parent frame again under this round's procedure, which has not been done.

corrections.what: BibTeX parser in acl_search.py appended uncollected field lines (pages, isbn) to the preceding collected field, corrupting 1886 of 10066 recorded DOIs.
corrections.found_by: auditing the pool before committing, not by a failing test
corrections.effect: 7 records that should have merged did not. Unique records 10066 -> 10059, duplicates removed 1296 -> 1303. Query hit counts and screening set unchanged.
corrections.also: DOI fields are now normalised at both ingest sites, which removed a Google Scholar session token that a PubMed record carried inside its doi ArticleId.

corrections.what: Screening decisions were recorded as positions in the priority ordering.
corrections.effect: The parser fix left the 487-record priority set identical but moved 29 positions. Decisions are now keyed by record title in include-candidates.json and screen.py resolves them, so a re-run cannot silently reassign a decision to another record.

corrections.what: The flow reported identification only from the database search; the sources that entered through other routes (known sources, professional guidance, citations) were not shown as such, and the synthesis counts predated the additions of 2026-09-13 (K28, K29, ME17, one assessment level, one blind spot, P13, P14).
corrections.effect: other_methods block added; full_text counts include the two guidance documents now logged; synthesis counts recomputed from the registry.

corrections.what: flow-v1 counted retrieval attempts as reports, listed Keren 2026 (S19) as not retrieved after its PDF had been logged, showed S4 under search and screening although it is not in the pool, carried two retrieved rows without file or checksum, and never recorded that S15-S17 were retrieved.
corrections.effect: flow.json is generated by build_flow.py from reports.json and the search, pool, screening and amendment records: full text is counted at report level (19 sought, 18 retrieved, 1 not retrieved) with attempts reported separately; the other-methods block is derived from the routes in the ledger; hand edits fail the suite.

corrections.what: build_pool.py read a PubMed record's DOI as the last ArticleId of type doi anywhere in the record, which includes the cited-reference list; 2719 PubMed records were keyed by a reference's DOI and distinct records merged as duplicates.
corrections.effect: Pool rebuilt with each record's own DOI: 10223 unique records (was 10059), 1139 duplicates removed (was 1303). Re-prioritised with the same rule and threshold: 507 records in the priority stratum (was 487), of which 20 entered it after the AI screen and are listed as not screened, never as excluded; remainder 9716 (was 9572). The audit judgement of 2026-09-13 is unchanged and its estimate is recomputed over the new remainder: 291 [134-621] clearly eligible (was 287 [132-612]).
